summary: This report covers a FOURTEEN-day window (2026-08-28 to 2026-09-11) because the 9/4 run crashed before publishing; nothing in it has ever been delivered to anyone. 31 messages, 11 from Alanna — her highest client volume since week one — and the two halves tell opposite stories. First half (8/28-9/4): the first invoice finally cleared on 8/30 after four chases and an explicit ultimatum from Stephski ('We will unfortunately have to pause work if it remains unpaid by the morning'), Stephski then fixed the invoicing defect herself by putting a 7-day term on invoice #2 (9/1), Mica Vecco broke a 28-day silence, and Alanna made the first expansion request of her life ('Would it possible to start more instas for me?') which Michelle answered in 11.5 hours. Second half (9/4-9/11): the recovery did not hold. Every single one of the three things the 9/4 state file named as next week's tests failed. (1) Ollie Mckinlay did not come back. His last message on this account is 2026-08-27 06:31 — he has now sent ZERO messages in fifteen days and zero in this entire fourteen-day window, while owning nine of the open commitments including all scene-drop work. (2) Invoice #2 was NOT paid by its stated 9/8 due date. It is now 3 days past the term Stephski herself set and 10 days from issue, with no chase since 9/5, and invoice #3 is due around 9/15 on top of it — the exact condition the last report defined as high payment risk. (3) The Drive uploads still have not happened, though Michelle chased a third time on 9/10 and Alanna proposed a real workaround ('Would it be possible to take stuff from my Dropbox instead?') that was still unanswered at window close, with Mayson pinging an unidentified handle @sotom225. The one genuine break in the pattern: on 9/8 Michelle delivered the first leak-removal report the account has ever received — 27 days after Derrek promised weekly reports, and delivered by promo rather than by Derrek or the DMCA function. Meanwhile the client keeps feeding the machine: on 9/10 she dumped 5000+ new photos 'to post on my wall and x' — page content, Ollie's job — and at window close nobody has acknowledged it. Her pinned release schedule ran out on Aug 29 and is 13 days exhausted with nobody asking for the next dates, after three consecutive uncovered drops (Aug 17, Aug 24, Aug 29). She is paying for OnlyFans page management and has received none of it for two weeks.

health.rationale: Down 12 from the 70 scored on 2026-09-04, and this drops her out of the healthy band she was the only client in. The 9/4 score of 70 was explicitly conditional — it was held up by billing, promo and social while the core service was dark, with the note that 'if Ollie stays absent another week this reverses immediately and harder than it rose'. He stayed absent. Zero messages from the page and chatting manager across the entire fourteen-day window and fifteen days total; the Aug 17/24/29 pinned drops are all uncovered; the pinned schedule is 13 days exhausted with no replacement requested; her 8/19 'stop chatting' instruction is 23 days unacknowledged; and on 9/10 she handed over 5000+ new page photos into an empty room. Money went the wrong way too: invoice #1 needed 15 days, four chases and a work-pause threat, and invoice #2 has now blown through the 7-day term Stephski herself introduced with no chase on or after the 9/8 due date. Mica relapsed to silence after one week (last message 8/31, 11 days). Derrek has not posted since 8/12 — 30 days. What holds the score at 58 rather than lower is that the client is not disengaging: 11 messages, an expansion request, a payment, an apology, a 5000-photo content handover and a self-proposed workaround, plus real delivery from Michelle including the first-ever leak report on 9/8 and a proactive IG warm-up status update. That is a client leaning in hard against a service that is not there. That gap is what churn looks like one month before it happens.

She is still the best operator on this account by a distance and she authored the 7-day term herself, which makes the unenforced deadline the more serious gap: a term with no chase behind it teaches the client the term is decorative.
